raw_response:
I’m farming only 1.1 mu, so I won’t do anything fancy this year. The land is small, our cash is tight, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I mainly follow what has worked on my own field and what the better farmers nearby do. For wheat, I still want a steady stand and good tillering, so I’ll sow on time in October, use an improved local seed, put most of the phosphate at the base, and split the nitrogen into base fertilizer and one topdress at jointing. Wheat usually pays back fertilizer better, so I won’t cut it too much. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is very tight, so I’ll keep it simple: harvest wheat, do shallow land prep or direct seeding quickly, use hybrid seed, and give enough fertilizer to hold yield but not so much that I spend too much cash. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I’ll irrigate wheat more because it responds clearly, and maize only if rain is short. I’d rather stay with a stable, familiar plan than gamble on big changes.
